newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel wants MTNL free from controls.
newsitem.headline: India panel wants MTNL free from controls.

text.p: The Indian government's Disinvestment Commission said on Friday that telephone giant Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) must have more autonomy to face up to coming competition from private firms.

"Considering its impressive track record over the past 10 years, the commission considers it a strong performer and recommends full autonomy to the board of directors...," it said in a report presented to the government on Thursday.

The commission, set up last year to advise on privatisation strategies, recommended that MTNL, which has a monopoly in Delhi and Bombay, make a Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) issue of 10 percent of the government stake.

"After the GDR issue, a domestic offer of the balance 28.3 million shares consisting of 4.73 percent equity may be made to institutional investors, and to individual investors at a 10 percent discount to the institutional price," the report said.
MTNL operates three million lines out of a total of 13.1 million lines in India, and has a potential consumer base of 23 million people.

The commission said it currently recommended the sale of 49 percent of MTNL's government stake, but a further sell-off could be considered once the industry sees the rise of private competitors over the next three to four years.
India began the process of ending a decades-old monopoly in basic telephones in 1994.

MTNL has already sold off 34.27 percent of its shares to the public, leaving a balance of 14.73 percent, or around 88 million shares, which can be sold off under the current partial privatisation programme.
The timing of the GDR issue of 60 million shares could be decided by experts, keeping in view the market conditions, the report said.

MTNL's 1996/97 (April-March) net profit rose to 8.87 billion rupees ($247.77 million) from 7.27 billion rupees in 1995/96. Sales increased to 39.6 billion rupees from 34.48 billion rupees in the previous year.
Analysts have predicted a 25 percent increase in the company's 1997/98 net profit.

"MTNL has always been a prime candidate for government divestment and now is as good a time as any," Sonal Jhaveri, telecoms analyst at brokerage HSBC Batlivala and Karani Securities Ltd, said earlier this week. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
